points.description: States that sizeof returns a size measured in bytes (e.g. 'the size in bytes', 'how many bytes it takes up', 'the byte size'). A bare 'the size' with no mention of bytes earns part marks only.
points.partial_credit: Partial share for saying only 'the size'/'how big it is' without indicating bytes.

levels.says: Says it returns the size/how big something is, but does not say the size is counted in bytes.

points.description: States that the size returned is that of its operand — i.e. of the value, variable, expression or type given to the operator (e.g. 'of its operand', 'of the thing passed to it', 'of the variable or data type').
points.partial_credit: Partial share if the answer only says it applies to 'a variable' or 'a data type' without the general idea of an operand/argument.

levels.says: Mentions only one kind of thing it applies to (e.g. only variables, or only data types) rather than the operand/argument in general.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both ideas: the result is a size in bytes, and that size is the size of the operator's operand. An answer that says only 'the size' without bytes, or that names only variables or only types, earns part marks on the relevant point. An answer about something else entirely (e.g. the number of elements, or the memory address) earns nothing.
